ci.inertReason: Which changed paths are allowed to shrink a CI run. This list is an ALLOW-LIST and the default is the full suite: a changed path matching nothing here forces `verify-browser` + `verify-integration` to run and every `verify:self` lane to run. That direction is the whole safety property — a new package, a new top-level directory, or a file nobody classified is covered by default, and no catch-all rule has to be remembered. Adding an entry is the only way to make anything skippable, which is why this file is code-owned (.github/CODEOWNERS) and why touching it lands in `ciConfig` below and forces a full run on its own PR. Never invert this into a list of paths that DO trigger things.

inert.reason: The agent pipeline. Safe to isolate for two independent reasons: knip.json ignores `scripts/**` entirely, so it cannot affect the dead-code gate, and nothing under packages/ imports it (it is a standalone npm package outside the pnpm workspace, which is why `verify:fast` never reaches it).

Prose. Maps to the entropy lane rather than to nothing because entropy.docStaleness.designDir below is `docs/design`, so a design-doc edit genuinely can fail that gate. Root-level `*.md` only — the single `*` does not cross a separator, so packages/README.md is deliberately NOT matched and falls through to a full run.
Agent-facing instructions. Read by Claude Code, executed by no lane. Empty tags means a .claude-only PR runs no verify:self lane at all.

The VitePress docs site. A workspace package, but a leaf one: nothing imports @wafflebase/documentation, so it cannot reach the engines, the frontend, or the browser/integration jobs. It is called out explicitly because it is one of the two packages/ entries that are genuinely inert, and because publish-ghpage.yml builds it at deploy time — the `documentation:build` lane exists so a broken docs build fails CI rather than the deploy.

The dev-only design-system editor Vite plugin, and wafflebase's own instance of it. Both are leaf packages: packages/frontend's vite.config.ts registers neither, so nothing they do can change what verify-browser renders or what verify-integration serves — both are `private: true` and neither enters a production bundle. NOTE, changed by the PR that added design-sandbox: it is no longer true that nothing in the workspace depends on @wafflebase/design-editor — design-sandbox does, which is the dogfood that proves the package boundary holds. That edge is inert-to-inert and does not reach the frontend, so the conclusion is unchanged, but the old wording read as evidence rather than as a claim about leaves. Both are analysed by knip (design-editor since #819), so the `designEditor` tag is claimed by four lanes: `design-editor:build`, `design-editor:check`, `design-sandbox:check` (the latter two tsc --noEmit + vitest) and `verify:entropy`, which carries the dead-code gate a change here can genuinely fail. Skipping entropy would have hidden dead code until main's push run. Both check lanes are tagged, because design-sandbox consumes design-editor through its `exports` map: a change to either can break the other's typecheck. `design-editor:build` is tagged for the reverse reason — since #966 that map names `dist/plugin/index.js`, so the sandbox's typecheck AND knip (which loads the sandbox's vite.config.ts) need the build, and both reach it through a `needs` edge on any package change. An inert entry whose tag no lane claims is strictly worse than not listing the path at all, so check the claimants when editing this.

ci.ciConfigReason: The gating surface itself. A change to any of these forces a full run, so a PR can never use the filter to grade its own homework — the reduced-run decision is always made by the version of the mapping already on main. It also drives the loud `ci-config-changed` label and job-summary warning, because CODEOWNERS only binds when branch protection has 'Require review from Code Owners' switched on.

Keeping upstream's own splitting is the point: a note with a `flowchart` fence downloads `mermaid.core` (~618 kB) plus that one diagram module, not the whole ~2.5 MB engine — folding it all into one `manualChunks` vendor chunk would triple the bytes for the common case and risks coupling the shared deps (katex is already in `notes-view`, d3 in recharts) into an eagerly-loaded chunk. Largest new chunk is 691 kB (`cynefin-*`), under the unchanged 710 kB global per-chunk cap, so no KB override was needed. The sanitizer that guards the rendered SVG (`dompurify`, ~20 kB) is loaded next to the engine rather than statically, so it stays off `notes-view-*.js` and costs at most one further deferred chunk — mermaid already depends on it, so it is bytes a diagram was paying for anyway. docStaleness.advisoryReason: Two shapes, both requiring a `reason`. `pattern` downgrades every finding in the design docs whose relative path it matches — for a spec whose whole subject is unbuilt. `doc` + `ref` downgrades one named reference and is the shape to prefer, because the rest of that doc keeps blocking: a doc carrying a planned-file name today still fails on real drift tomorrow. Nothing here is silent — every advisory finding is printed on every run, prefixed `(advisory)`. These are not refs anyone forgot to fix: a design doc that names a file in order to say it does NOT exist ("there is no `mixed-controls.tsx`") is doing its job, and rewriting it to satisfy the checker would delete accurate documentation.

advisory.reason: The design-editor docs specify an editor UI that is still unwritten. `packages/design-editor` now holds the server core (`src/server/{extract,inject,stamp,jsx-nodes}.mjs`), the plugin host (`src/plugin/**`) and the token seam (`src/tokens/**`); `packages/design-sandbox` now exists and holds the `@wafflebase/core` token adapter, the scene manifest and the live-server smoke script. What is still spec-only is the shell UI and the scene runtime — `src/editor/**`, `src/scenes/**`, `providers.tsx`, the fixtures and the canvas shims — which PRs 10-12 create. So the remaining references name files the spec intends to create, and a spec for unbuilt work is not a stale doc; failing on it would repeat the false positive this check was fixed for. Narrow this to `doc` + `ref` entries as the UI fills in, and drop it once the refs resolve.
